correctness.rationale: With all affine parity-check labels used once, two-window syndromes are exactly zero, all Q odd-parity single-column syndromes, and even-parity adjacent differences. Telescoping XOR forces a missing difference in any noncyclic ordering; a repeated-difference XOR forces one in any cyclic ordering. The primitive power list omits precisely u=1+alpha^{-1}; a power-exponent argument exhibits that missing u as a two-apart difference, within a three-window, for each m>=2. The embedded standalone checker directly enumerates syndromes for m=2..11 and every m=3 ordering. Computations corroborate but are not used to prove the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The 2026 burst-covering paper identifies position ordering as material and proves a single length-eight case. The finding settles coordinate-optimized burst radius for the entire extended binary Hamming family in both cyclic and noncyclic models, gives a deterministic primitive-element construction, and establishes the exact best syndrome accessibility under two consecutive positions. This is a structural all-length classification of the optimum parameter, directly motivated by contiguous-access coding rather than an arbitrary finite table.
